what_it_does: Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) is a technique where an AI model, before answering a question, first searches a large external knowledge base to find relevant passages and uses them as context. As these knowledge bases grow to billions of documents, they no longer fit in fast memory chips and must live on NVMe solid-state storage drives — which are much slower. This paper identifies that the search-and-retrieval step (converting the question into a numeric representation, searching the database, and reading the matching records off storage) has become the main bottleneck for how fast the overall system responds. The proposed solution is a programmable accelerator chip embedded directly inside the storage device itself, so that search and even the conversion of the query into numbers can be done right where the data lives, without shipping huge amounts of raw data over the slow connection to the main server. The accelerator is flexible enough to handle several different database index structures used in practice.
